_comment: Tappable body regions. ids are side-agnostic; the figure has L/R prims that map to the same id. 'joint' names the rig articulation whose DOF the viewer shows when this region is tapped.

regions.label: Head
regions.anatomy: Skull, jaw, face. Cranks lever the head to load the cervical spine; chokes are set up by head position (chin strap, cross-face).
regions.plain: Your head and jaw. Cranks use the head as a handle to bend or twist your neck, and head position sets up most chokes (chin strap, cross-face).

regions.label: Neck
regions.anatomy: Cervical spine (C1–C7), carotid arteries and jugular veins (blood chokes), trachea (air chokes).
regions.plain: The neck bones, the arteries on the side of the neck (blood chokes cut blood flow to the brain) and the windpipe (air chokes).

regions.label: Shoulder
regions.anatomy: Glenohumeral joint, rotator cuff, anterior capsule. Rotational locks (kimura, americana, omoplata) attack it.
regions.plain: The shoulder joint, its rotator cuff and the shoulder blade. Twisting locks (kimura, americana, omoplata) crank the shoulder past its range.

regions.label: Upper arm
regions.anatomy: Humerus, biceps brachii and brachialis — the bicep slicer compresses these against a fulcrum.
regions.plain: The upper-arm bone and the biceps. The bicep slicer crushes these muscles against a bone used as a wedge.

regions.label: Elbow
regions.anatomy: Humeroulnar joint, ulnar collateral ligament, anterior capsule. Hyperextension locks (armbar) attack it.
regions.plain: The elbow joint and the ligaments on its inside. Armbars bend the elbow the wrong way (hyperextension).

regions.label: Forearm
regions.anatomy: Radius/ulna, pronation–supination. Common grip point for kimura, americana and wrist locks.
regions.plain: The two forearm bones that let the palm turn up and down. A common grip point for the kimura, americana and wrist locks.

regions.label: Wrist
regions.anatomy: Radiocarpal joint and carpal ligaments. Wrist locks flex, extend or rotate it past range.
regions.plain: The wrist joint and its small ligaments. Wrist locks bend or twist the wrist past where it can go.

regions.label: Hand
regions.anatomy: Carpals/metacarpals and fingers. Grip-fighting target; finger locks are illegal in IBJJF.
regions.plain: The hand and fingers. Mostly a grip-fighting target; finger locks are illegal under IBJJF rules.

regions.label: Chest
regions.anatomy: Thoracic spine, rib cage, sternum. Chest-to-chest pressure and the mount/side-control pins load it.
regions.plain: Ribs, breastbone and upper back. Chest-to-chest pressure in mount and side control squeezes it and makes breathing hard.

regions.label: Abdomen / spine
regions.anatomy: Lumbar spine, abdominal wall. Spinal locks (twister) and knee-on-belly pressure target it.
regions.plain: The belly and lower back. Spine locks (the twister) and knee-on-belly pressure target it.

regions.label: Hips
regions.anatomy: Pelvis, hip joints, adductors/groin. Hip control is the heart of pins and guard; the banana split attacks the adductors.
regions.plain: The hip joints, pelvis and groin. Hip control is the heart of pins and guard; the banana split stretches the groin.

regions.label: Thigh
regions.anatomy: Femur, quadriceps, hamstrings. Leg-entanglement controls (inside position, knee line) live here.
regions.plain: The thigh bone, quads and hamstrings. Leg-lock control (inside position, the knee line) is fought here.

regions.label: Knee
regions.anatomy: Tibiofemoral joint; ACL/PCL, MCL/LCL, menisci. Heel hooks rotate it; kneebars hyperextend it.
regions.plain: The knee joint, its ligaments (ACL, MCL and others) and cartilage. Heel hooks twist it; kneebars straighten it the wrong way.

regions.label: Shin / calf
regions.anatomy: Tibia/fibula, gastrocnemius and soleus. Calf slicers compress the calf against a fulcrum.
regions.plain: The shin bone and the calf muscles. Calf slicers crush the calf against a shin or forearm used as a wedge.

regions.label: Ankle
regions.anatomy: Talocrural and subtalar joints, Achilles tendon. Straight ankle locks and toe holds attack it.
regions.plain: The ankle joint and the Achilles (ankle) tendon. Straight ankle locks and toe holds attack it.

regions.label: Foot
regions.anatomy: Tarsals, metatarsals, toes. The grip point for toe holds and heel hooks.
regions.plain: The foot, heel and toes. The handle for toe holds and heel hooks.
